name: LCD2004 I2C 20x4 character LCD
description: 20-character by 4-line HD44780-compatible character LCD with an LED backlight, driven over I2C through a PCF8574 8-bit I/O expander backpack in 4-bit mode (P0 RS, P1 RW, P2 E, P3 backlight, P4-P7 D4-D7). Runs on 5 V. Sold as: LCD2004 20x4 blue character LCD with PCF8574T I2C backpack (FC-113 / HW-061 clone module), 4-pin header GND, VCC, SDA, SCL, I2C address 0x27 (0x3F on boards with a PCF8574AT), contrast trimmer and backlight jumper on the backpack.
eli5: A screen that shows four lines of twenty letters or numbers, wired with just four wires.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (LCD logic and backlight; 4.5-5.5 V)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7 kOhm pull-up to VCC fitted on the backpack)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 kOhm pull-up to VCC fitted on the backpack)

buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V: the HD44780 and the backlight are made for 5 V, and at 3.3 V the text is faint or invisible.

The backpack pulls SDA and SCL up to VCC (5 V) with 4.7 kOhm resistors. On a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico) remove those two resistors and use 3.3 V pull-ups, or put a bidirectional level shifter between them.
Turn the blue contrast trimmer on the backpack until the characters appear; with it wrong the screen shows nothing or a row of solid blocks.
Address 0x27 with a PCF8574T and the A0-A2 pads open; 0x3F if the chip is a PCF8574AT. Run i2c.scan() if nothing shows.
Keep the backlight jumper fitted, or the backlight cannot turn on.
Line starts in display RAM are 0x00, 0x40, 0x14 and 0x54, so row 3 continues row 1 and row 4 continues row 2 if you write past 20 characters.

driver.code:
# LCD2004 (HD44780-compatible 20x4 character LCD) on a PCF8574 I2C backpack.
# Backpack wiring: P0 = RS, P1 = RW, P2 = E, P3 = backlight, P4-P7 = D4-D7 (4-bit mode).
# Init sequence and timings from the Hitachi HD44780U datasheet (Figure 24, 4-bit interface).
import time

_RS = 0x01
_RW = 0x02
_EN = 0x04
_BL = 0x08


class LCD2004:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x27, cols=20, rows=4):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.cols = cols
        self.rows = rows
        self.bl = _BL
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([0]))  # all port lines low, E low
        time.sleep_ms(50)  # > 40 ms after VCC rises to 2.7 V
        self._nib(0x03, 0)
        time.sleep_ms(5)  # > 4.1 ms
        self._nib(0x03, 0)
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # > 100 us
        self._nib(0x03, 0)
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self._nib(0x02, 0)  # switch to 4-bit
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self.cmd(0x28)  # function set: 4-bit, 2 lines (4-row panels use N=1), 5x8 dots
        self.cmd(0x08)  # display off
        self.clear()
        self.cmd(0x06)  # entry mode: increment, no shift
        self.cmd(0x0C)  # display on, cursor off, blink off

    def _w(self, b):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([b | self.bl]))

    def _nib(self, n, rs):
        b = ((n & 0x0F) << 4) | rs
        self._w(b | _EN)  # E high (each I2C byte takes ~90 us at 100 kHz, > 450 ns PWEH)
        self._w(b)  # E falling edge latches the nibble

    def _byte(self, v, rs):
        self._nib(v >> 4, rs)
        self._nib(v & 0x0F, rs)

    def cmd(self, c):
        self._byte(c, 0)
        if c <= 0x03:
            time.sleep_ms(2)  # clear / return home take 1.52 ms
        else:
            time.sleep_us(50)  # other instructions take 37 us

    def clear(self):
        self.cmd(0x01)

    def home(self):
        self.cmd(0x02)

    def move_to(self, col, row):
        # DDRAM start of each line on a 20x4 panel: 0x00, 0x40, 0x14, 0x54
        base = (0x00, 0x40, self.cols, 0x40 + self.cols)[row]
        self.cmd(0x80 | (base + col))

    def putchar(self, ch):
        self._byte(ord(ch), _RS)
        time.sleep_us(50)

    def putstr(self, s):
        for ch in s:
            self.putchar(ch)

    def backlight(self, on=True):
        self.bl = _BL if on else 0
        self._w(0)

    def display(self, on=True):
        self.cmd(0x0C if on else 0x08)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from lcd2004_i2c import LCD2004

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
lcd = LCD2004(i2c, 0x27, 20, 4)
lcd.move_to(0, 0)
lcd.putstr('Hello, Sparkbench!')
lcd.move_to(3, 3)
lcd.putstr('Count: 42')
print('LCD ready')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
